summary: The settled way for an application to talk to a headset or a pair of glasses: it covers the session, the frame loop, the tracked spaces, the views to draw, the input actions and touch feedback. It is a ratified Khronos standard with a real conformance test suite and an adopter programme, and the current release is 1.1.63, dated 2 September 2026, so read the version line before you cite it. There are two builds of the same document: one with all ratified extensions and one with all registered extensions, and the second says of itself that it is not a ratified specification. Of the 253 extensions in the registry only 52 are ratified, all 29 Khronos-tagged ones and 23 of the 39 multi-vendor ones, and not one single-vendor extension is ratified. It draws nothing itself: an application cannot even open a session without one of the ratified graphics binding extensions, and there is no sound, no scene, no networking and no identity anywhere in it. Two traps for a standards audience: the nine ratified spatial extensions, the first six of them ratified in June 2025, give you anchors, planes, markers and persistence but no way to share an anchor with another device or another person, and the only two audio extensions in the whole registry are single-vendor and unratified, so the ratified specification has no audio surface at all.

coverage.note: It draws nothing. It hands the application a chain of images to draw into with a graphics interface of the application's choosing, then composites the submitted layers back to front. Turning geometry into pixels happens entirely outside it.
